articles.title: Quer ser doador de órgãos? Veja como registrar vontade pela internet | G1
articles.standfirst: Mais de 300 sul-mato-grossenses já registraram a intenção de doar órgãos pelo serviço desde 2024; no país, mais de 49 mil pessoas aguardam por um transplante.
articles.summary: Mais de 300 sul-mato-grossenses já registraram a intenção de doar órgãos pelo serviço desde 2024; no país, mais de 49 mil pessoas aguardam por um transplante.
articles.body:
Doação de órgãos pode ser registrada pela internet em MS — Foto: Reprodução

Quem deseja ser doador de órgãos pode registrar a intenção pela internet, de forma gratuita, por meio da Autorização Eletrônica de Doação de Órgãos (AEDO). O serviço permite formalizar a vontade de doar e indicar quais órgãos, tecidos ou partes do corpo a pessoa deseja disponibilizar para transplante.

Em Mato Grosso do Sul, 380 pessoas fizeram o registro desde o lançamento da ferramenta, em 2024. Foram 275 solicitações naquele ano, 76 em 2025 e outras 29 em 2026, segundo os dados mais recentes da plataforma.

A AEDO foi criada pelo Colégio Notarial do Brasil – Conselho Federal (CNB/CF), por meio da plataforma e-Notariado, e regulamentada nacionalmente pelo Conselho Nacional de Justiça (CNJ). O procedimento pode ser feito de casa, sem a necessidade de comparecer a um Cartório de Notas.

Mais de 49 mil pessoas aguardam transplante

O serviço está disponível em um cenário de alta demanda por transplantes no país. Dados do Ministério da Saúde divulgados neste mês apontam que mais de 49 mil pessoas aguardam atualmente por um transplante no Brasil. Cerca de 45 mil estão na fila por um rim.

Entre os pacientes que aguardam um transplante de córnea, são 37.719 pessoas, segundo levantamento do Conselho Brasileiro de Oftalmologia (CBO). O número é 15% maior que o registrado em dezembro de 2025.

Outro desafio para a doação é a autorização da família. No Brasil, a retirada de órgãos após a morte depende da concordância dos familiares, mesmo quando a pessoa manifestou em vida o desejo de ser doadora.

A taxa média de recusa familiar está em torno de 45%. Entre os motivos apontados estão o desconhecimento da vontade do potencial doador e dúvidas ou receios sobre o procedimento.

Conforme o presidente do Colégio Notarial do Brasil - Seccional Mato Grosso do Sul, Elder Dutra, é nesse ponto que a AEDO busca contribuir, ao deixar registrada a decisão da pessoa.

“A principal contribuição da AEDO é permitir que uma intenção muitas vezes expressada apenas verbalmente fique documentada. Em Mato Grosso do Sul, cada nova autorização também funciona como um convite para que o tema seja discutido de maneira clara entre o potencial doador e sua família”, afirma.

O procedimento é gratuito e feito integralmente pela internet. O interessado deve acessar a plataforma da AEDO, disponível no e-Notariado, preencher os dados e escolher um Cartório de Notas.

Depois, participa de uma videoconferência com o tabelião para confirmar a identidade e a vontade de fazer a doação. O documento é assinado eletronicamente e passa a integrar a Central Nacional de Doadores de Órgãos.

A autorização pode ser consultada por profissionais autorizados do Sistema Nacional de Transplantes. O cidadão também pode escolher quais órgãos, tecidos ou partes do corpo deseja doar e revogar a autorização a qualquer momento.

articles.title: Nevoeiro interrompe movimentação no maior porto da América do Sul | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo o Climatempo, o nevoeiro segue na cidade de Santos (SP) pela manhã, perde força à tarde e retorna no período noturno.
articles.summary: Segundo o Climatempo, o nevoeiro segue na cidade de Santos (SP) pela manhã, perde força à tarde e retorna no período noturno.
articles.body:
Um nevoeiro encobriu a cidade de Santos , no litoral de São Paulo, neste sábado (26). O fenômeno foi responsável pela paralisação das navegações no Porto de Santos e das travessias litorâneas da região, devido à baixa visibilidade provocada pela nebulosidade.

De acordo com a Praticagem de São Paulo, o Canal do Porto foi fechado às 3h20 para navegações. Conforme a última atualização no portal da entidade, às 8h05, as navegações seguiam suspensas.

De acordo com a Secretaria de Meio Ambiente, Infraestrutura e Logística (Semil), as travessias litorâneas já retomaram a operação, em razão da melhora da visibilidade, na manhã deste sábado (26), por volta das 8h.

Durante a madrugada, foram registrados fechamentos temporários nas travessias de balsa em Cananéia/Continente, Cananéia/Ilha Comprida, Santos/Guarujá, Vicente de Carvalho/Santos e Guarujá/Bertioga, segundo a Semil.

Imagens obtidas pelo g1 mostram um navio vermelho em meio ao nevoeiro no terminal do Porto de Santos. O registro foi feito no início da manhã deste sábado, durante a travessia de passageiros entre Guarujá e Santos.

Nevoeiro interrompeu a navegação no Porto de Santos, SP, na manhã deste sábado (26) — Foto: Daniel Gois

O g1 entrou em contato com a Capitania dos Portos e com a Autoridade Portuária de Santos (APS) para atualizações sobre a situação do Porto, mas não havia obtido retorno até a última atualização desta reportagem.

Segundo o Climatempo, a previsão indica que o nevoeiro deve persistir durante a manhã e retornar no período noturno, sem força durante à tarde.

As temperaturas durante este sábado variam entre 26ºC e 17ºC, com predominância de tempo ensolarado à tarde. Não há previsão de chuva para este sábado e a expectativa aponta que os ventos não ultrapassam 25 km/h.

articles.title: Alunos da rede pública de Bauru e Marília vão fazer intercâmbio | G1
articles.standfirst: Projeto ‘Prontos pro Mundo’ oferece intercâmbio em países como Austrália, Canadá, Irlanda e Nova Zelândia. Em Bauru, 25 alunos de escolas estaduais foram aprovados e em Marília, 29 estudantes.
articles.summary: O programa Intercâmbio Prontos pro Mundo selecionou 54 alunos da rede estadual de Bauru e Marília para estudar no exterior com todos os custos pagos pelo Governo de SP.
articles.body:
Mais de 50 alunos de escolas da rede estadual das regiões de Bauru e Marília (SP) vão ter a oportunidade de estudar por três meses em escolas de países como Austrália, Canadá, Irlanda e Nova Zelândia. Eles foram aprovados no programa “Prontos pro Mundo” e embarcam para o intercâmbio em 2027. ( Saiba mais sobre o programa abaixo no fim da reportagem ).

Na região de Bauru foram 25 alunos selecionados e já em Marília, 29 estudantes, totalizando 54 aprovados.

A estudante Izabela de Oliveira, de 17 anos, aprovada no programa em 2025, viveu a experiência de estudar na Nova Zelândia. Em entrevista ao g1 , a estudante conta que além de estudar as matérias comuns do ensino médio, ela também pode participar de excursões e passeios pelo país, além de aprender mais sobre a cultura do país.

“Foi incrível! Um sonho realizado que eu nunca vou me esquecer. Ainda no aeroporto, eu estava um pouco assustada com como minha vida estava mudando, mas em nenhum momento senti medo ou vontade de desistir. Tive o apoio de uma família anfitriã maravilhosa, que me acolheu como uma filha. E tudo saiu melhor do que eu poderia imaginar”, afirma.

Izabela, estudante de Bauru, ficou três meses na Nova Zelândia — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

O intercâmbio é sem custo para os alunos da rede estadual e um dos pré-requisitos para participar do programa é realizar a prova do Saresp, que avalia o rendimento escolar. Izabela conta que se preparou bastante para o exame e também foi selecionada para um curso de inglês.

“Durante o curso, continuei me preparando como se o intercâmbio fosse uma certeza, e por fim acabou sendo”, destaca.

Para a jovem, que é aluna da Escola Estadual Henrique Rocha de Andrade, a experiência de viver em outro país foi muito importante para o crescimento pessoal.

“Acho que a parte mais importante é a forma como depois de tudo isso, o mundo parece muito pequeno. Todos os sonhos parecem possíveis, e as oportunidades parecem melhores. Mas não foi o mundo que mudou, foi eu mesma. Eu amadureci, aprendi a estar longe de tudo que eu conheço e com toda certeza essa foi a parte mais importante.”

Izabela com os colegas durante o intercâmbio na Nova Zelândia — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

O Canadá foi o destino da estudante Helena Teles de Oliveira, que também foi selecionada no programa de intercâmbio. A preparação para morar e estudar por três meses no país contou com várias experiências de vivência com a língua inglesa, que é um dos idiomas oficiais do Canadá.

“Desde o nono ano eu já me preparava bastante para realizar o Saresp, que é uma avaliação que está nos critérios do programa, e eu tinha uma frequência alta na escola, faltava raramente. Depois de descobrir que havia sido selecionada, eu realizei o curso de inglês oferecido pelo programa, e ao longo do ano continuei criando uma imersão na língua inglesa. Via filmes e séries todos em inglês. Comecei a acompanhar influencers estrangeiros, e troquei o idioma do meu celular, para ter contato diário com a língua”, conta em entrevista ao g1 .

Helena destaca ainda que durante a experiência de intercâmbio pode vivenciar a cultura local como festivais de música, o halloween e o dia de Ação de Graças, que são bem tradicionais no país.

“Foi a melhor experiência da minha vida. A adaptação foi tranquila, me senti muito acolhida. Eu aprendi muito com todos que conheci e tive experiências que me fizeram crescer muito. Sinto que depois que voltei eu me tornei uma pessoa mais confiante, comunicativa e independente”, completa a aluna da Escola Estadual Professor Francisco Alves Brizola.

Helena, aluna da rede estadual em Bauru, fez intercâmbio no Canadá — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Durante os três meses, os estudantes frequentam escolas locais — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Com 16 anos, Rafaela da Silva Almeida, também coleciona as experiências e aprendizados do intercâmbio. Ela morou e estudou por três meses em uma escola da Irlanda. Momentos especiais que ela “guarda na memória”.

“Tudo o que eu vivi, desde as pequenas coisas do dia a dia até as grandes experiências foram marcantes para mim. Na hora, eu nem percebia como aqueles momentos eram especiais, mas agora que acabou, sinto saudades”, confessa.

A jovem também conta que apesar da distância de estar em um país em outro continente, com língua, costumes e climas diferentes, não teve medo de não se adaptar.

“Não tive muito medo de não conseguir me comunicar ou me adaptar, estava aberta a novas experiências e para mim foi algo tranquilo. Minha host family me apoiava e me ajudava a compreender melhor o inglês no dia a dia, as conversas simples que fazem a diferença, acho que estar imersa no idioma é uma das melhores formas de aprender.”

Para os estudantes que também tem essa meta de realizar um intercâmbio, a estudante aconselha: “Eu acho que o conselho principal é realmente não ter medo de tentar. Quando eu me inscrevi, nem achava que seria aceita, mas pensei ‘por que não?’. Essa é uma daquelas oportunidades que realmente vale a pena agarrar. E se você tiver a oportunidade de ir, se permita conhecer coisas novas e aproveite o máximo que puder, porque depois você vai sentir falta até das pequenas coisas”, conclui.

Rafaela, aluna de Bauru, fez intercâmbio na Irlanda — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Para 2027, foram oferecidas 500 vagas de intercâmbio para o primeiro semestre escolar dos países que fazem parte do programa. Por ano, o projeto leva 1 mil estudantes para experiência High School (semelhante ao Ensino Médio) em países de língua inglesa, em dois períodos de seleção por ano, no primeiro e segundo semestre.

Os 54 alunos de Bauru e Marília embarcam para o período de três meses de intercâmbio no segundo semestre de 2027.

Concorreram às 500 vagas do intercâmbio nessa etapa mais de 50 mil estudantes matriculados na 1ª série do Ensino Médio da rede estadual. São classificados para a prova de seleção, os alunos que apresentam os seguintes requisitos:

Frequentam a rede pública de ensino desde o 6º ano do Ensino Fundamental;

Fizeram o Saresp no ano passado, quando estavam matriculados no 9º ano do Ensino Fundamental;

Fizeram o curso de inglês oferecido pelo programa;

Foram aprovados na prova de proficiência em língua inglesa;

Obtiveram frequência escolar a partir de 90% no primeiro semestre deste ano nas aulas regulares;

Registraram nota 7 ou superior em todas as disciplinas da matriz curricular.

Os estudantes chamados são divididos em duas listas: por município e classificação geral. Inicialmente, o Prontos pro Mundo classifica um estudante representante de cada município paulista.

As vagas das cidades sem alunos aptos a concorrer pelo intercâmbio foram destinadas à distribuição pelos principais critérios do programa (nota do Saresp e nota da prova do Prontos pro Mundo) por ordem de classificação.

O intercâmbio do Programa Prontos pro Mundo é 100% gratuito para o aluno e sua família, com todos os custos e organização providenciados pela Seduc-SP. Itens como documentos pessoais (passaporte, visto), hospedagem, aulas, traslados, passagens aéreas serão cobertos.

Durante estadia no exterior, alunos também são beneficiados com uma bolsa-auxílio para despesas pessoais.

Irlanda é um dos destinos dos intercâmbios do Programa Prontos pro Mundo — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

articles.title: Pampulha terá trecho da orla fechado para lazer aos sábados | G1
articles.standfirst: Iniciativa da Prefeitura de Belo Horizonte reserva 3,4 quilômetros da Avenida Otacílio Negrão de Lima para pedestres, ciclistas e praticantes de atividades físicas das 7h às 13h.
articles.summary: Iniciativa da Prefeitura de Belo Horizonte reserva 3,4 quilômetros da Avenida Otacílio Negrão de Lima para pedestres, ciclistas e praticantes de atividades físicas das 7h às 13h.
articles.body:
Trecho de 3,4 km da orla da Lagoa da Pampulha ficará exclusivo para pedestres, ciclistas e praticantes de atividades físicas aos sábados. — Foto: PBH

A orla da Lagoa da Pampulha passa a contar, a partir deste sábado (26), com um espaço exclusivo para lazer, esportes e convivência . Toda semana, um trecho de 3,4 quilômetros da Avenida Otacílio Negrão de Lima para atividades ao ar livre, sempre aos sábados, das 7h às 13h.

Segundo a Prefeitura de Belo Horizonte , agentes da BHTrans e da Superintendência de Mobilidade do Município (Sumob) atuarão na operação de trânsito, realizando os bloqueios, orientando motoristas e garantindo a segurança dos usuários da via. A proposta é ampliar as opções de convivência e ocupação dos espaços públicos da cidade.

Motoristas que precisarem circular pela região deverão utilizar outras vias.

Sentido Parque Ecológico: o desvio será feito pelas avenidas Cremona e pelas ruas Palermo e Sardenha.

Sentido Mineirão: o trajeto poderá ser realizado pela Rua Sardenha, Rua Palermo e Avenida Cremona.

A prefeitura informou que o acesso de moradores e comerciantes às garagens será mantido durante a interdição.

A linha 5106 (Bandeirantes/BH Shopping) terá mudanças temporárias no itinerário e nos pontos de embarque e desembarque durante o fechamento da avenida. Os passageiros poderão solicitar embarque e desembarque ao longo do percurso dos desvios.

Os patinetes elétricos também poderão ser utilizados na região durante a ação. Atualmente, a Pampulha conta com 20 estações do serviço, sendo quatro delas localizadas dentro do trecho reservado ao projeto.

O serviço é permitido apenas para pessoas com 18 anos ou mais e deve ser utilizado de forma individual.

Orla da Pampulha terá área livre para pedestres, ciclistas e para quem usa patinetes elé — Foto: Divulgação/Prefeitura de Belo Horizonte

articles.title: Ricardo Corbucci come 5 kg de fast food em São Vicente | g1 | G1
articles.standfirst: Ricardo Corbucci consumiu 5 kg de fast food durante desafio em São Vicente. Influenciador contou ao g1 como começou a produzir vídeos com grandes quantidades de comida.
articles.summary: Ricardo Corbucci, do canal Corbucci Eats, consumiu 5 kg de lanches em um shopping de São Vicente e revelou como mantém a rotina entre os desafios de comida.
articles.body:
O influenciador Ricardo Corbucci enfrentou um desafio de consumir 5 kg de fast food de diferentes restaurantes da praça de alimentação de um shopping em São Vicente , no litoral de São Paulo. Corbucci conclui a prova em 22 minutos e 39 segundos.

O desafio aconteceu na noite de sexta-feira (25), no Brisamar Shopping. O evento contou com a participação do público, que pôde tentar adivinhar em quanto tempo Corbucci concluiria a prova.

O influenciador é responsável pelo canal Corbucci Eats, que reúne mais de 10 milhões de seguidores nas redes sociais. Ao g1 , ele disse que, apesar da quantidade de desafios dos quais costuma participar, tenta diversificar os conteúdos.

"Atualmente, o que eu mais busco é fazer os vídeos com maior entretenimento para as pessoas, que elas gostem de assistir, que elas tenham prazer em assistir. Não necessariamente são vídeos de recorde hoje em dia", afirmou.

Ricardo Corbucci enfrentou um desafio de consumir 5 kg de fast food em São Vicente, SP. — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

Corbucci ganhou projeção na internet ao registrar desafios envolvendo grandes quantidades de comida e competições contra o relógio. O influenciador contou que a ideia surgiu depois de um desafio em Brasília, quando precisou comer 3 kg de açaí em 30 minutos.

“Eram 3 kg de açaí em meia hora e eu comi em 4 minutos”, relembrou.

A partir daquele desafio, ele começou a pesquisar sobre a produção de conteúdo nesse formato e passou a publicar os vídeos em 2016. O bordão “Bora que eu tô com fome” surgiu por acaso, durante uma gravação, e acabou sendo adotado após uma sugestão de um seguidor.

Corbucci concluiu o desafio em 22 minutos e 39 segundos. — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

Ao longo da carreira, Corbucci já acumulou alguns recordes:

🌭 43 hot dogs em um campeonato nos Estados Unidos, em 10 minutos;

⏱️ O maior volume de comida que consumiu foi 8,4 kg de melancia em 30 minutos.

Para se preparar, ele conta que faz jejum antes e depois dos desafios, além de manter uma rotina de treinos físicos e uma dieta restrita nos dias em que não está gravando.

Corbucci comeu 5 kg de fast food. — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

Com o crescimento do canal, Corbucci afirmou que pretende diversificar o conteúdo e não ficar restrito a provas para bater recordes. Segundo ele, a ideia é produzir vídeos mais voltados ao entretenimento, sem deixar de lado os desafios com grandes quantidades de comida.

“Quero fazer uma redução de danos para não precisar ficar sempre batendo recorde, comendo cada vez mais”, explicou.

Corbucci publica vídeos de desafios com grandes quantidades de comida. — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

articles.title: Pakistan govt puts Islamabad on lockdown as Imran Khan’s party pushes ahead with march
articles.summary: Leaders of former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party have vowed to press ahead with nationwide demonstrations
articles.body: Leaders of former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party have vowed to press ahead with nationwide demonstrations demanding his release, as authorities tightened security in Islamabad ahead of the planned march.More than 1,000 shipping containers, many reinforced with spikes, have been placed to block roads, while sandbags have been positioned on bridges and a key highway leading into the capital has been closed. Public gatherings have also been banned in Islamabad, with 22,000 police and other security personnel deployed across the city.The government has also deployed security personnel in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and closed the main highway linking the provincial capital, Peshawar, with Islamabad. The sweeping security measures have fuelled anger and frustration in the capital, with several businesses struggling to receive supplies.The measures to prevent Khan’s PTI from proceeding with the march come amid mounting concerns over the treatment of the former prime minister, who has been in jail since August 2023 following convictions in multiple cases.On Friday, PTI leaders announced that they would postpone the start of the march to October 4, a week after the original September 27 date, saying they hoped the delay would put further pressure on the government.The planned protest also comes amid the detention of three of Imran Khan’s sisters. articles.title: Royal Navy bomb experts given highest humanitarian honour
articles.summary: The squadron made a 500kg WW2 bomb safe during four days of disruption in Plymouth in 2024.
articles.body:
Royal Navy divers, who safely dispose of hundreds of bombs, shells and explosive devices every year, have been awarded the military's highest humanitarian award.

Bravo Squadron of the Diving and Threat Exploitation Group, which is split between Portsmouth and Devonport Naval Bases, was given the Firmin Sword of Peace during a ceremony at the Hampshire base for its work throughout 2024.

Earlier this week in Falmouth, the unit moved an unexploded World War Two bomb out to sea, where it will be detonated next week.

The award is given to units that have made the most valuable contribution towards establishing good relations with a community at home or abroad.

In February 2024, thousands of people were evacuated in Plymouth as the unit safely removed and disposed of a 500kg (1,102lb) WW2 bomb at sea.

City roads were closed and trains stopped as the bomb was moved by the experts.

The then defence secretary, Grant Shapps, praised the squadron's "bravery and fortitude" and those involved in the "highly complex operation".

In December 2024, it safely removed a 1,000kg (2,204lb) WW2 bomb discovered in Southsea after it was dug up by an excavator during work on new sea defences.

Other work that year saw the squadron join patrol ship HMS Tamar and sail to Pitcairn in the Pacific Ocean, where demolition charges left from the construction of the island's harbour were removed over two days.

Commanding Officer Lt Cdr Benjamin Brown said the squadron's work "embodies the very spirit of the Firmin Sword of Peace: selfless service, protection of life and humanitarian impact".

He added: "At home and abroad, Bravo Squadron demonstrates courage, professionalism and compassion, standing as a genuine force for good.

"In combating a lethal explosive legacy, the squadron is eminently deserving of the award, recognising its extraordinary and enduring contribution to peace and public safety."

articles.title: 'Padma Bhushan small thing, make him PM': Cong mocks BJP Bengal chief's praise for CEC
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Congress leader Pawan Khera on Saturday hit back at West Bengal BJP chief Samik Bhattacharya after the latter said Chief Election Commissioner
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Congress leader Pawan Khera on Saturday hit back at West Bengal BJP chief Samik Bhattacharya after the latter said Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar deserved the Padma Bhushan for his role in conducting the state’s recent assembly election and revising the voter list.Reacting to Bhattacharya’s remarks, Khera said, "The Padma Bhushan is a very small thing. Make him the Prime Minister. After all, a person who can make others Prime Minister should be made one himself."Bhattacharya had earlier praised the CEC while speaking to reporters at Panihati in North 24 Parganas district, saying the CEC deserved the Padma Bhushan "at the very least". He credited Kumar with ensuring a violence-free election in West Bengal and with "cleansing" the electoral roll by removing illegal Bangladeshi immigrants."Gyanesh Kumar deserves to be awarded, at the very least, with the Padma Bhushan. The people of West Bengal are delighted that, after so long, intimidation was kept at bay, that there were no incidents of murder during the elections and people were actually allowed to cast their votes," the BJP leader said.He also claimed that Kumar had played a key role in the revision of the voter list."In a border state like West Bengal, Gyanesh Kumar took the initiative to remove the names of Bangladeshi infiltrators from the voter list," Bhattacharya said."The people of West Bengal have rarely witnessed an election like this. Therefore, the general public of West Bengal is grateful to Gyanesh Kumar and has blessed him with all their hearts," he added.The BJP leader’s comments came amid a growing controversy over the functioning of the Election Commission during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise. An Indian Express report said that two election commissioners had objected to decisions allegedly taken in their names have triggered criticism from the Opposition.Also read:Unease within NDA over EC-SIR row? Three BJP allies seek poll body clarification as opposition keeps up pressureCongress has held nationwide protests demanding Kumar’s removal and arrest, while a plea has also been filed in the Supreme Court challenging election-related orders and alleged software changes attributed to the CEC without the concurrence of the other two election commissioners.The row has also drawn criticism from Rahul Gandhi, who accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah and Kumar of being "traitors" and alleged that they were destroying the foundation of India’s democracy by rigging elections.Bhattacharya, however, dismissed Gandhi’s remarks, saying, "The Congress itself doesn't pay heed to him. His own party doesn't take him seriously, and you are talking of Rahul Gandhi."Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) has a reminder for immigrants in the country asking them to report a change of address to the agency
articles.body: US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) has a reminder for immigrants in the country asking them to report a change of address to the agency within 10 days of moving, warning that failing to update the address could lead to missed notices, delays in immigration cases and problems receiving immigration documents. The immigration authority shared the reminder on X (formerly Twitter), also making clear that changing an address with the US Postal Service does not automatically update records with USCIS.“Changing your address with USPS does not update your address with USCIS, and USPS will not forward USCIS mail. You are responsible for keeping your address current with both USCIS and USPS. If you do not update your address with USCIS, you may miss notices, your case may be delayed, and you may not receive your immigration documents,” the agency wrote.The post also has a link to the USCIS webpage detailing the process of address change. Here’s what it saysHow to change your address with USCISIf you have filed an immigration benefit request with USCIS, you must notify USCIS of any changes of address as soon as possible to ensure you receive all correspondence and benefits without delay. Additionally, all aliens in the United States must report a change of address to USCIS within 10 days of moving. This reporting requirement does not apply to A and G visa holders and visa waiver visitors.We strongly encourage you to submit your change of address through a USCIS online account as soon as you move.Changing your address with the U.S. Postal Service (USPS) will not change your address with USCIS and USPS will not forward your mail from USCIS. Please update your information with both USCIS and USPS. We recommend you use the USPS Look Up a ZIP Code tool to ensure that you give USCIS your full address using the standard abbreviations and formatting recognized by USPS.How to change your address with USCIS onlineUsing an online account to update your address in a timely way meets the legal requirement to notify us that you have moved. It also ensures that your case will continue processing without interruption and that you receive all correspondence and benefits without delay. Changing your address online allows us to process your change of address almost immediately and eliminates the need to file a paper Form AR-11, Alien’s Change of Address Card, by mail.Most people can change their address online using the USCIS Enterprise Change of Address (E-COA) self-service change-of-address tool. This tool can be found in their USCIS Online Account under the My Account dropdown menu. If you do not have a USCIS online account, see our How to Create a USCIS Online Account page. Some people may not have access to this feature, see the Specific Procedures for Certain Populations section for more information.If you have a pending, approved, or previously filed case with USCIS, you may change your address using your USCIS online account even if you initially filed your benefit request by mail.NOTE: If you use your USCIS online account to change your address, you must enter the receipt numbers for each pending benefit request to apply the address change. Providing receipt numbers helps ensure that we update your address where needed and that you continue to receive important correspondence and benefits related to these cases from USCIS without delay.How to change your address with USCIS by mailYou also may file a paper Form AR-11 by mail to change your address. This meets the legal requirement to notify USCIS of a change of address. However, because filing a paper-based Form AR-11 does not provide for an automated update to your address in USCIS systems, we strongly encourage requestors to use the self-service change of address tool available in their USCIS online account when reporting a change of address.You use AI every day. articles.title: Sean Connery's former French Riviera 'James Bond House' was extensively renovated and once tried the market at €30 million; the six-level Nice villa's asking price was cut to €18.5 million in May 2026
articles.summary: On the French Riviera, few homes can claim a past quite as cinematic as Villa Le Roc Fleur.
articles.body: On the French Riviera, few homes can claim a past quite as cinematic as Villa Le Roc Fleur. Perched above the Mediterranean in Nice, the Art Deco residence was once home to Sean Connery, the actor who made James Bond synonymous with a certain kind of effortless glamour. Decades later, the six-level villa is back on the market, carrying both its Hollywood history and a significantly lower price, states the latest report by Mansion Global. The property is now asking €18.5 million (US$21.48 million), after previously appearing on the market for as much as €30 million.A home with a 007 connectionKnown locally as the James Bond House, Villa Le Roc Fleur became Connery's French Riviera base during the 1970s and 1980s. He shared the residence with his wife, Micheline Roquebrune, during the years when his career was closely associated with the Bond franchise. The report also states that the house gained another connection to the character when it appeared in the 1983 film Never Say Never Again. The movie marked Connery's seventh and final appearance as the British secret agent, giving the property a place in Bond history as well as in the actor's personal story.The villa stands at the foot of Mont Boron, overlooking the seafront and the Mediterranean. Its setting gives the property sweeping views while placing it within one of the French Riviera's most recognizable landscapes.From €30 million to €18.5 millionThe property has tested the market at several price points, including €30 million and €23.5 million. Its latest asking price was reduced to €18.5 million in May 2026 as the sellers sought to reposition the estate for renewed interest from international buyers, adds the Mansion Global report.The current owners have carried out extensive renovations, updating the interiors, finishes and technical infrastructure while expanding the home's wellness and leisure amenities. Despite the modernization, the renovation has retained many of the architectural elements that give the villa its period character.Art Deco character meets modern luxuryBuilt in 1930, the main residence offers more than 10,000 square feet of living space spread across six levels. Its interiors retain details associated with the home's original design, including mosaic inlays, wood paneling, wrought-iron banisters, decorative ceiling moldings and the original elevator cabin.The outdoor spaces are equally central to the property. Multiple terraces overlook the Mediterranean, while a rooftop deck includes a barbecue area designed for entertaining against the Riviera skyline.The leisure facilities bring the estate firmly into contemporary luxury territory. There are indoor and outdoor swimming pools, a hammam, gym, spa and home theater, along with a wine cellar.A private Riviera compoundBeyond the main house, the property includes a separate two-bedroom caretaker's apartment and a guest house of nearly 2,000 square feet. Together, the buildings create a private compound rather than simply a single residence. For prospective buyers, however, the most distinctive feature may remain the story attached to the address. Nearly a century after its construction, Villa Le Roc Fleur combines preserved Art Deco details, sweeping Mediterranean views and a chapter in Sean Connery's Bond legacy, now offered at a price well below its earlier €30 million market attempt, concludes the online report.Images Courtesy: Wikipedia and Mansion GlobalReady to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: 'October 7 attack equal to sixteen 9/11s': Israeli PM Netanyahu in UN speech
articles.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the October 7, 2023, Hamas attack was, in proportionate terms, equivalent to 16 September 11 attacks in the
articles.body: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the October 7, 2023, Hamas attack was, in proportionate terms, equivalent to 16 September 11 attacks in the United States.Recalling the attack, Netanyahu said Hamas militants had killed about 1,200 people in Israel, including civilians, and abducted 251 others.“These Hamas monsters, they slaughtered Holocaust survivors. They burned babies alive in front of their parents. They beheaded our men. They brutally raped our women. And then they murdered them. Altogether, they slaughtered 1,200 Israelis that day. I want to give you an idea of what this means for a country of 10 million. Proportionately, this is equal to 40,000 innocent Americans slaughtered in less than 24 hours. That's 16 times 9/11. 16 9/11s that occurred not very far from here. On that darkest of days, our enemies expected us to collapse. Well, we didn't collapse. Instead, we rose and fought like lions.”Netanyahu's remarks came after days of speeches from world leaders condemning Israel’s war in Gaza and accusing his government of genocide against Palestinians. He rejected the allegations, calling Israeli genocide claims “the biggest lie of the century”.His appearance was marked by a mass walkout, with scores of delegates leaving the chamber as he approached the rostrum. Netanyahu responded by calling those who left “moral cowards”.“In defending itself, Israel is also defending many of the countries whose delegates just left this hall,” Netanyahu said. “In fact, I want you to know that many of their leaders even thank us privately for taking out Iran’s nukes.”He also defended Israel’s decision to attack Iran, saying it was “one of the easiest decisions I’ve ever had to make”, and thanked US President Donald Trump for his actions against Tehran.Netanyahu's speech also addressed violence by Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank, which he described as involving a “handful of young juvenile delinquents”. He said, “I can’t stand that. I won’t stand for vigilantism,” while accusing foreign leaders and international media of exaggerating the scale of the violence.His address came as Israel faced growing international criticism over its conduct of the Gaza war. According to the Gaza Health Ministry, at least 73,922 Palestinians have been killed in Israel’s subsequent offensive, while Israel maintains control over large parts of the territory and continues military operations.You use AI every day. articles.title: Russia to launch drone strike on Europe? CIA warns of 'potential' threat
articles.summary: The Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) has warned European governments about a possible Russian plan to launch drones from commercial vessels in the
articles.body: The Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) has warned European governments about a possible Russian plan to launch drones from commercial vessels in the Mediterranean, with Spain, France and Italy reportedly among the potential targets. The alleged operation could involve drones being concealed aboard merchant ships and launched from international waters towards targets along the European coast.According to a report by Spanish newspaper El Mundo, the suspected Russian operation would use commercial vessels as covert drone launch platforms, with the drones reportedly targeting airports, ports and other critical infrastructure.The drones could reportedly be hidden inside shipping containers and launched from the vessels using a compact catapult system, allowing them to approach European targets from the sea. The reported aim would be to cause disruption and damage rather than carry out a large-scale conventional attack.The drone at the centre of the reported operation is the Russian Gerbera, a relatively small unmanned aircraft that has been used by Russian forces in the war in Ukraine. According to Defense News, the drone has a wingspan of about 2.5 metres and a reported range of up to 600 km.The Gerbera is designed as a low-cost, lightweight drone and has also been used as a decoy to complicate Ukrainian air-defence operations. Its relatively small size could make it easier to transport and conceal aboard commercial vessels, which is central to the reported Mediterranean scenario.Also read: Russia targets Ukraine's digital nerve centres as war reaches data infrastructureWhy the threat could be significantThe reported threat could be significant because it would potentially allow drones to be launched from commercial vessels operating among normal maritime traffic, making the launch platform harder to identify and monitor.The use of international waters could further complicate detection and attribution. European authorities would have to monitor not only their airspace but also a large number of civilian vessels moving across the Mediterranean.The Gerbera's reported range of up to 600 km could also give such vessels considerable flexibility in choosing a launch position. A drone launched offshore could approach European targets from an unexpected direction, potentially challenging existing air-defence and surveillance systems.The threat also raised concerns about disruption rather than sheer destructive power. Even a relatively small drone striking an airport, port, energy facility or other critical infrastructure could temporarily halt operations, cause economic losses and create wider public-security concerns.

articles.title: “Just get up and walk out”: Elon Musk’s unusual meeting rule for Tesla employees and why he called staying when you add no value ‘rude’
articles.summary: For many employees, leaving a meeting before it ends can feel awkward.
articles.body: For many employees, leaving a meeting before it ends can feel awkward. Even when the discussion has little to do with their work, people often stay until the meeting is officially over because walking out may appear disrespectful. Elon Musk once described a very different approach. During a conversation at the 2015 Edison Electric Institute (EEI) Annual Convention in New Orleans, Musk spoke with Edison International Chairman, Ted Craver about Tesla, electric vehicles and the changing energy industry. Musk discussed Tesla's approach to meetings and said that employees who had nothing to contribute could leave.“We also have a rule that if somebody's in a meeting and finds that this meeting is not helping them in a meaningful way and they are not contributing to the meeting, they should just leave,” Musk said. He then gave a very direct instruction: “Just get up and pack. Just get up and walk out, all right.” Craver asked whether doing that would be considered rude in Tesla's workplace culture. “And would that be, in your culture, would it be rude to do that?” “No, that's expected,” said Musk. Then he added: “It's rude to stay.” During the same conversation, Musk explained the reasoning further. If someone was simply looking at their phone or laptop during a meeting, he said, they could do that at their desk instead. He also described meetings as “a big time suck.”Musk later put the same idea in a Tesla memoMusk returned to the subject three years later in an email to Tesla employees. The April 2018 message came as Tesla was working to increase Model 3 production, and Musk included a section of recommendations on productivity. The email resurfaced after an X user shared it in an X post to which Musk replied in an affirmative yes. His first recommendation concerned large meetings. “Excessive meetings are the blight of big companies and almost always get worse over time,” Musk wrote. He advised employees to get rid of large meetings unless they were certain that the meetings were providing value to everyone attending. If such a meeting was necessary, he said it should be kept very short. He also addressed meetings that happen repeatedly. “Also get rid of frequent meetings, unless you are dealing with an extremely urgent matter,” Musk wrote. “Meeting frequency should drop rapidly once the urgent matter is resolved.”His advice went beyond meetingsThe 2018 email also addressed how Tesla employees communicated with one another. Musk told employees that communication should take the shortest route necessary to get a job done rather than automatically moving through a management hierarchy. “Communication should travel via the shortest path necessary to get the job done, not through the ‘chain of command,’” he wrote. He also warned against using internal acronyms and terminology that required employees to learn additional vocabulary simply to understand their colleagues. “Don't use acronyms or nonsense words for objects, software, or processes at Tesla,” Musk wrote. “In general, anything that requires an explanation inhibits communication.” He explained the reason in practical terms, “We don't want people to have to memorize a glossary just to function at Tesla.”You use AI every day. articles.title: In 1775, fruit jars were sealed under George Washington’s floor; 249 years later, archaeologists opened the site and found 29 bottles intact with whole cherries inside
articles.summary: A recent excavation at George Washington's Mount Vernon revealed 35 glass bottles from the 18th century, 29 of which contained preserved cherries and other fruits. This significant find offers insights into 18th-century food storage and historical food practices at the estate.
articles.body: Archaeologists were excavating George Washington’s Mount Vernon mansion and discovered 35 glass bottles from the 18th century, and 29 of them were still intact with preserved fruit inside. The bottles were found in five storage pits in the mansion’s cellar during the $40 million Mansion Revitalization Project. Most contained cherries, while some of the fruit was identified as likely gooseberries or currants. The bottle shapes are characteristic of styles from the 1740s and 1750s, and Mount Vernon says the bottles may have been forgotten in the pits.The contents were carefully removed from the bottles and placed under refrigeration, and the glass was prepared for conservation. The discovery followed an earlier find in the cellar of two intact European-made bottles containing liquid, cherries and pits, and together, the finds gave archaeologists a rather well-preserved collection of biological material from Mount Vernon’s 18th-century household.What was inside the bottlesEarly analysis of the fruit found 54 cherry pits and 23 stems, along with cherry pulp. Researchers found that the stems had been neatly cut and deliberately left attached to the fruit before it was placed in the bottles, with microscopy suggesting that the cherries may have been harvested by snipping them from trees with shears.Mount Vernon says that the cherries are likely to have been a tart variety, and their higher acidity may have helped preserve the fruit, although researchers are still examining the material. The pits are also being tested to determine whether any remain viable for germination, while DNA analysis could eventually help identify the precise variety of cherry.Documentary records show that wine, whiskey and brandy were kept there, along with turnips, potatoes, butter, beef and pork, and the newly discovered bottles therefore fit into a wider picture of how the Washington household stored food. Mount Vernon also has a recipe for Cherry Bounce, which is a brandy-based cherry drink that was popular in the 18th century and known to have been enjoyed by George Washington. Researchers have not established that the newly discovered cherries were intended for Cherry Bounce, so the purpose of these particular bottles remains uncertain.The people behind the foodMount Vernon has connected the discovery to the enslaved people who managed food production and preparation at the estate, including Doll, who was a cook brought to Mount Vernon by Martha Washington in 1759 and was charged with overseeing the kitchen.The careful preparation of the cherries is one reason archaeologists are interested in the discovery, since the cut stems, preserved pits and fruit pulp provide physical evidence of how the food was handled before it was stored. Mount Vernon Principal Archaeologist Jason Boroughs said that the material could contribute to research into 18th-century foodways, the environment and the origins of American cuisine.Mount Vernon has partnered with the US Department of Agriculture’s Agricultural Research Service to analyze the contents. Only a small quantity of the samples had been analyzed when the initial findings were announced, which leaves further questions about the fruit, its variety and its preservation.Researchers are still examining the fruitScientists are examining whether any remain viable for germination, while DNA testing may help researchers compare the fruit with databases of heirloom varieties, which could help establish whether the cherries belonged to a variety that is still known today or one that has disappeared. Researchers can examine the fruit itself, rather than having to rely solely on written recipes or descriptions from the period. The physical evidence includes the fruit, pits, stems and the glass containers in which they were stored.Archaeological investigations have accompanied parts of the work that require digging around the mansion, which gave researchers access to areas that have rarely been examined. The cellar is expected to remain part of the ongoing archaeological and preservation work as Mount Vernon prepares for the next phase of the mansion’s restoration.The preserved fruit has become archaeological evidence of what was grown, prepared and stored at Mount Vernon, almost three centuries after the bottles were made. The remaining analysis could determine more about the cherries themselves and the food practices of the people who prepared them.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 'What is going on inside EC?' Union ministers, BJP allies call on poll body to clarify SIR row
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Union minister HD Kumaraswamy on Saturday called on the Election Commission EC to clarify amid the continuing row over the Special Intensive
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Union minister HD Kumaraswamy on Saturday called on the Election Commission EC to clarify amid the continuing row over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Kumaraswamy said the responsibility for addressing reports of internal differences lay with the Election Commission itself and that the country needed to know what was actually happening within the constitutional body.“It is not the question of demands by any party or any leader. The responsibility of the Election Commission, that is important. What is the ground reality? What is going on inside the Election Commission?” Kumaraswamy said.His remarks came a day after three NDA allies Chirag Paswan's LJP(RV), Upendra Kushwaha's RLM and Chandrababu Naidu's TDP separately urged the Election Commission to address concerns surrounding the SIR exercise and reports of differences within the poll panel.Kumaraswamy said there was a need to distinguish between reports appearing in the media and the actual situation inside the ECI.“The difference between what we are watching in the media and what is the real fact has to come out by these members. Because this is an important organisation, an autonomous body; why has it happened? That reality they must tell the media and the country. Their responsibility is greater. It is not an easy thing. Those three Election Commission members, including the chairman, what is the problem between them? What is the fault in that? Anything is there, they have to spell it,” he said.The issue gained traction after The Indian Express reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had recorded 14 written dissents or objections over a 10-month period. The reports have prompted opposition demands for action against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and calls to halt the SIR process.The ECI has maintained that differing views, internal notes and queries are part of its institutional functioning and said its final decisions on the SIR were unanimous. What NDA allies saidLJP(RV) chief and Union minister Chirag Paswan on Friday said he did not intend to “defend what is a constitutional body” but argued that the Election Commission should address public concerns directly.“If questions are being raised about its conduct, it is the responsibility of EC, especially the chief election commissioner (Gyanesh Kumar), to present its side firmly,” Paswan said.He added: “If people start losing trust in the electoral system, that will not augur well for democracy and, therefore, I think the EC must come out with its clarification more forcefully. It need not respond to what Rahul Gandhi and his associates are saying. But it must dispel misgivings in the minds of the people.”RLM president Upendra Kushwaha also called for an immediate clarification, writing on social media, “There is considerable confusion among the public regarding the controversy surrounding SIR. This issue needs to be addressed. The EC should immediately clarify the situation to dispel this confusion.”The TDP too sought greater transparency. TDP parliamentary party neta Lavu Sri Krishna Devarayalu said, “The EC is a constitutional institution entrusted with a crucial responsibility in our democracy. Therefore, whenever questions are raised by anyone, providing appropriate clarification and maintaining transparency will only help strengthen public confidence in the institution.”Opposition raises allegationsMeanwhile, Jharkhand Minister Irfan Ansari criticised Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the SIR exercise and alleged that names had been removed from electoral rolls.Speaking to ANI, Ansari alleged that the ECI had acted in a manner that benefited the BJP and questioned whether the poll panel would work according to the directions of a political party. The allegations were not independently established in his remarks.“I want to ask the citizens of the country, and I even want to ask the BJP voters: Names have been removed from the voter list; your name might have been removed too,” Ansari said.He also alleged that names of Muslims, Dalits and Adivasis had been deleted from voter lists and demanded that elections in Bihar be held again.“The Commission is an independent, neutral body. No political party should interfere with it,” he said, while alleging that Kumar had interfered and helped the BJP.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: In 2026, Houston opened the nearly $30 million Hill at Sims, turning a 100-acre flood basin into a park that holds 325 million gallons of stormwater for Sunnyside
articles.summary: In May 2026, Houston's Hill at Sims opened, transforming a 100-acre flood basin into a dual-purpose park for recreation and stormwater storage, benefiting over 50,000 residents in Sunnyside.
articles.body: Houston's Hill at Sims opened in May 2026 on a site that was designed to hold stormwater. The 100-acre park in the Sunnyside neighborhood sits on a Harris County Flood Control District detention basin with nearly 325 million gallons of storage capacity. The $30 million project adds trails, a hilltop pavilion, a pedestrian bridge and other public amenities without negating the site's original flood-control function.The Houston Parks Board managed the project with Harris County Precinct One and the Flood Control District, and describes Hill at Sims as a dual-purpose park. The detention basin remains part of the region's stormwater infrastructure, while the surrounding space is now open for recreation. The park is at 11808 Scott Street along Sims Bayou and connects with the wider Sims Bayou Greenway trail network.A flood basin became a public parkHouston Parks Board began working with Harris County Commissioner Rodney Ellis and the Flood Control District on transforming the 100-acre detention basin into a regional park in 2021. The completed park has nearly 4.5 miles of new hike-and-bike trails, which include a 1.6-mile loop and nature trails. A new pedestrian and bicycle bridge crosses Sims Bayou and links the park to the greenway on the opposite side, and the site also includes a water-access pier, picnic areas, a nature pavilion with restrooms and a hilltop pavilion.A 60-foot hill that provides views toward downtown Houston is the park's defining physical feature. The site also contains six large-scale murals created through a partnership with Street Art for Mankind, and more than 670 native trees were supplied through partnerships involving Texas Parks and Wildlife and Trees For Houston. Water can collect in the detention basin rather than immediately moving downstream through the drainage system during heavy rainfall, and the new trails and recreation areas were designed around that infrastructure rather than replacing it.Axios reported that the basin can hold nearly 325 million gallons of stormwater and that the park serves more than 50,000 residents in Sunnyside and south Houston. The project was funded through a combination of public and private money, with about $22 million coming from public funding, while the Houston Parks Board secured nearly $8 million in private investment from The Brown Foundation.The park opened after years of planningHouston Parks Board says more than 20 community meetings were held and more than 700 residents contributed feedback during the planning process. The property functioned primarily as a detention basin rather than a conventional public park before the conversion, and the completed project added places to walk, cycle, fish and gather while the basin was available for its original purpose. The design also incorporates trails, gathering areas and public amenities around the basin without removing its flood-management capacity, which allowed recreation and stormwater infrastructure to occupy the same site.Hill at Sims also forms part of a larger greenway system, and the new pedestrian bridge connects the park to Sims Bayou Greenway, which Houston Parks Board says will eventually extend nearly 20 miles between Blue Ridge County Park and Milby Park. The park's opening in May 2026 therefore did not mark the end of the flood basin's original job, and the same 100 acres now perform two functions of storing stormwater during severe weather and providing trails, open space and recreation for the surrounding Sunnyside community.You use AI every day. articles.title: Meet Lidia Rak, the 18-year-old Florida student whose research found a correlation between groundwater radium and pediatric brain-tumor incidence; her school says her advocacy contributed to a $30 million state bill
articles.summary: At 18, Lidia Rak has already taken her interest in cancer research beyond the classroom and into conversations with lawmakers.
articles.body: At 18, Lidia Rak has already taken her interest in cancer research beyond the classroom and into conversations with lawmakers. The Mandarin High School senior began looking at cancer data after a personal experience with an autoimmune blood condition led her to learn more about cancer risks. Her research eventually turned towards pediatric brain tumours and the possible relationship between naturally occurring radium in groundwater and reported cases in Florida. Rak then began advocating for greater attention to childhood cancer research and care. According to her school, Mandarin High School, that work also contributed to a $30 million Florida bill supporting local hospitals.How Rak's research beganRak told Duval County Public Schools that her research started with leukemia and cancer data. She had been interested in blood conditions because of her own childhood diagnosis of an autoimmune blood condition, which she said increased her risk of developing cancer. While looking at cancer cases in Florida, her focus eventually shifted to brain tumours. The turning point came when she was reading research about possible cancer clusters in the Jacksonville area. The earlier work had examined whether airborne carcinogens could help explain the clusters but had not found a statistically significant connection. Rak noticed that the researchers had not examined possible waterborne carcinogens. That gap prompted her to ask a different question: could something in the water be associated with the pattern of pediatric cancer cases?She began examining available data and looking specifically at radium levels in groundwater alongside pediatric brain-tumour incidence. According to Rak's account to her school, her analysis identified a correlation between the two. The distinction between correlation and causation is important here. Rak's research identified a statistical relationship in the data she examined; that finding by itself does not establish that groundwater radium causes pediatric brain tumours. Her school describes the work as an environmental epidemiology study.From student research to cancer advocacyRak did not stop with the research. She began using what she had found to talk about pediatric cancer funding and support. As a National Gold Together Ambassador for the American Cancer Society, she has spoken with lawmakers in Florida and Washington, DC. She told Mandarin High School that her conversations with legislators were not simply about presenting statistical figures. Instead, she tried to explain the presence of cancer clusters in the Jacksonville area and why she believed more attention should be given to pediatric cancer research and patient support.Her interest in childhood cancer is also tied to what she sees as a gap between pediatric and adult cancer care. According to Rak, she became more aware of differences in funding while working as a national ambassador for the American Cancer Society. The Barron Prize for Young Heroes also recognised this combination of research and advocacy when it named Rak among its 2026 winners. The prize described her work as an independent environmental epidemiology study examining the relationship between naturally occurring radium in drinking water and pediatric brain-tumour incidence in Florida. It also said she had used the research to advocate for increased pediatric cancer research funding.What the $30 million bill means in her storyRak's advocacy has also taken her into state policy discussions. Mandarin High School reported in April that she had contributed to a $30 million Florida bill supporting local hospitals. The school described this as one of the outcomes of her work as a student researcher and advocate. For Rak, the policy work grew out of a broader concern about how pediatric cancer is researched and treated. She told her school that childhood cancer may receive less funding than adult cancers despite the long-term effects that a diagnosis can have on children.Her advocacy has therefore gone beyond her original research question. The groundwater-radium project gave her one way to examine a potential environmental factor, while her work with the American Cancer Society gave her an opportunity to discuss pediatric cancer funding more broadly.What comes next for the 18-year-oldRak is planning to continue both her scientific and advocacy work. She told Mandarin High School that she intends to study molecular biology in college and eventually pursue medicine, with the goal of becoming a pediatric oncologist. She also plans to remain involved with the American Cancer Society and continue working on brain-tumour research. She is also working on a book about youth advocacy. Rak said the project is aimed at young people who want to get involved but may not know where to begin. She has spoken about her own experience of finding a starting point through a volunteer opportunity and gradually becoming involved in cancer advocacy.Her story has now earned recognition beyond her school and state. The Gloria Barron Prize for Young Heroes selected Rak as one of its 2026 winners, part of a group of 25 young people recognised for projects involving service, science, health and the environment.For Rak, the research and advocacy appear to be connected by the same goal: understanding issues that affect children and finding ways to draw greater attention to them. Her groundwater research offers a specific statistical association to investigate further, while her advocacy has given her a platform to push for more discussion and funding around pediatric cancer.You use AI every day. articles.title: He left studies after Class 12, suffered 1992 stock market scam; now Dinesh Thakkar owns an entire ₹711 crore Juhu tower in Mumbai
articles.summary: A Class 12 graduate who once chose business over conventional higher education is now making headlines for one of India’s most expensive residential
articles.body: A Class 12 graduate who once chose business over conventional higher education is now making headlines for one of India’s most expensive residential property purchases. Meet Dinesh Thakkar, founder, chairman and managing director of Angel One. In a recent news update, Thakkar has agreed to buy an entire residential tower in Mumbai’s Juhu for about ₹711 crore.Now that is not just any high-profile purchase about the price tag. It is also a story of a man’s unusual entrepreneurial journey. How a young man who entered the stock market, suffered heavy losses and faced the aftermath of the 1992 scam and still built one of India’s prominent retail broking platforms.From Class 12 to stockbrokingThakkar’s is not an ordinary story. As per profiles based on his own accounts, he studied till 12 class. He was born in Mumbai’s Mulund region and came from a business family involved in textile trading. He initially joined the family business but eventually decided to try his hand at the stock market.Thakkar has extensively spoken about borrowing money from friends to enter the market. An early bout of market volatility reportedly resulted in losses of around ₹6 lakh. Instead of walking away, he began looking more closely at how the broking business worked and what retail investors needed.That eventually took him from being a market participant to becoming a broker.1992 scamThe 1992 securities scam and the turmoil that followed left Thakkar heavily in debt, according to his account. The business survived with backing from three investors, who reportedly invested ₹50 lakh each.The company that eventually emerged from that journey was incorporated as Angel Broking in 1996. Angel One's own investor information lists August 8, 1996, as its date of incorporation and identifies Dinesh D. Thakkar as its founder, chairman and managing director.From traditional broker to digital financial platformAngel One began as a traditional stockbroking company. Over the years, it moved towards a technology-led model, with the company describing 2019 as the beginning of its digital journey with an end-to-end digital investment platform.That transformation mirrors the larger change in India's investment culture — from phone calls and physical paperwork to smartphones, digital onboarding and app-based trading.And decades later, after entering the financial markets, he is making headlines for a very different kind of transaction.₹711 crore for an entire tower, ‘Angelus’On September 22, 2026 Embassy Developments announced that it had signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Thakkar for the sale of an entire residential tower at Embassy Terazza in Juhu. The developer described it as India's largest single residential unit transaction.The tower is technically a G+7 structure, meaning ground plus seven upper floors, eight levels in all. It has a RERA carpet area of 63,000 sq ft and a transaction value of approximately ₹711 crore. That works out to roughly ₹1.13 lakh per sq ft based on the stated carpet area.Rather than buying one apartment in a luxury tower, Thakkar is taking an entire vertical slice of the development. He has named the residence ‘Angelus’.Why Juhu?“Juhu has always had a special character,” he said in a statement released by Embassy Developments.Embassy Terazza is located on Juhu Tara Road, one of Mumbai's established luxury residential addresses. The development is spread across more than two acres and has around 50 residences across five towers. Each tower has one residence per floor, with the project designed around privacy, sea and city views, landscaped spaces and wellness and lifestyle amenities.The project itself has an estimated gross development value of more than ₹3,000 crore.For a man whose career began with a Class 12 education, borrowed money, early market losses and a battered brokerage business, the purchase represents a striking chapter in a journey that has unfolded alongside India's transformation from traditional stockbroking to digital investing.You use AI every day. articles.title: Peter Thiel: Germany does not have a Mark Zuckerberg or Elon Musk, because the country is scared of ...
articles.summary: Billionaire investor Pete Thiel feels that Germany lacks global-scale entrepreneurs like Elon Musk or Mark Zuckerberg because the country suffers from a
articles.body: Billionaire investor Pete Thiel feels that Germany lacks global-scale entrepreneurs like Elon Musk or Mark Zuckerberg because the country suffers from a “fear of success.” He argues that German founders often exit early instead of scaling companies into global giants, leaving the nation behind in innovation and wealth creation. According to a report by Fortune, speaking on the MDMEETS podcast, Thiel said German entrepreneurs are not only risk-averse but also hesitant to embrace success at scale. “If you have something that works—you’re not going to scale it to this extreme degree like an Elon Musk or Mark Zuckerberg,” he explained. Instead, founders tend to sell or exit before their companies become truly global businesses.Thiel contrasted this with the US, where entrepreneurs aggressively expand successful ventures, creating thousands of jobs and new millionaires. He noted that Germany has produced few major new companies in recent decades, despite being Europe’s largest economy.Germany's standing in global business rankings continues to slipThiel's comments come as Germany's standing in global business rankings continues to slip. For the first time in the four-year history of the Fortune 500 Europe list, the UK has overtaken Germany as the country with the most companies represented, 76 to 73. Germany also lags in innovation more broadly — the country holds only a fraction of the unicorn startups found in the US and China, and ranked just 10th in the European Union's 2026 Innovation Scoreboard, trailing smaller economies like Austria, Luxembourg, and Ireland.Peter Thiel: Inherited wealth versus self-made wealth reveals a generational divideThiel also drew a sharper contrast between how wealth is generated among the richest people in Germany versus the US. By his own estimate, roughly a dozen of America's 50 wealthiest people are Gen X or younger, and most of them built their fortunes from scratch. In Germany, he counted around 20 people in that same age bracket among the wealthiest — but said, in his assessment, every single one of them inherited their wealth rather than building something new.He argued that the difference matters beyond personal wealth accumulation: each of the US entrepreneurs he pointed to didn't just build a fortune for themselves, but created thousands of millionaires among their employees and tens of thousands of additional jobs, contributing to the broader economy in the process — a ripple effect he suggested is largely missing in Germany's wealth landscape.Germany's industrial giants are struggling tooThiel's broader critique lands at a difficult moment for Germany's traditional economic engine: its automotive industry. Volkswagen, long Europe's largest company by revenue, ranked as high as No. 6 globally on the Fortune Global 500 in 2017, but has since fallen to No. 13, weighed down by its emissions scandal and intensifying competition from Chinese EV makers. The company recently approved a major restructuring plan that includes cutting its model lineup roughly in half and eliminating 50,000 jobs, on top of another 50,000 cuts already agreed to over the past two years — with its stock down more than 35% year to date.Volkswagen isn't alone in that struggle. Fellow German auto giants BMW and Mercedes-Benz, ranked No. 50 and No. 51 on the Global 500 respectively, have also seen their share prices fall more than 20% over the past year, reinforcing broader concerns about the country's economic competitiveness — concerns Thiel's comments suggest run deeper than any single industry's troubles.You use AI every day. articles.title: Watch: Eggs hurled, car window smashed as Kunal Ghosh heads to Mamata rally
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: TMC MLA Kunal Ghosh's car was pelted with eggs on Saturday while he was travelling to Serampore in Hooghly to attend a political rally
articles.body: NEW DELHI: TMC MLA Kunal Ghosh's car was pelted with eggs on Saturday while he was travelling to Serampore in Hooghly to attend a political rally addressed by former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee.The incident took place in the Uttarpara area, where a group of people carrying black flags surrounded Ghosh’s vehicle and shouted the slogan “go black”, a party leader said.The group pelted the TMC legislator’s car with eggs and stones, breaking its rear windshield.Reacting to the incident, Ghosh said, "This is jungle raj. They attacked my car with stones and eggs and blocked the road. No police personnel were present there. I am now returning to Kolkata and will go straight to Lal Bazaar or Bhawani Bhawan to lodge a complaint."TMC leaders alleged that the incident was the “handiwork of the BJP”.Mamata Banerjee is scheduled to address the public meeting later on Saturday.The rally at Serampore Court grounds had earlier faced legal hurdles before the Calcutta high court allowed the meeting, subject to conditions including a cap on attendance and police security arrangements.The incident comes amid a political standoff between the Trinamool Congress and police in Serampore ahead of the meeting. Police arrested two Trinamool volunteers, Sudip Acharya and Nur Islam, on Thursday in connection with extortion cases.A day before the rally, the TMC claimed that police had rounded up more than 150 party workers, including women, across the district. Serampore MP Kalyan Banerjee condemned the action. “Police have started a massive action against our workers and have rounded up more than 150 of them, including women. Despite this, a large number of people remain interested in attending Didi’s meeting,” he said.Following a meeting with local police officials on Friday, Asit Mazumdar, convener of Serampore district TMC, accused the police of disrupting party operations. “We submitted all required documents to comply with the HC order, but police started massive arrests, forcing most of our workers to flee,” Mazumdar said, questioning the justification behind targeting the event’s volunteers.Get the latest India News and Live updates.
